sources.title: Peoples of the Amur Region in the Early Middle Ages
sources.note: Russian Academy monograph description emphasizing an ethnogeographic reconstruction and debated correlations between named peoples and archaeological groups.

sources.title: The homeland of Proto-Tungusic inferred from contemporary words and ancient genomes
sources.note: Peer-reviewed language-family synthesis, disputed homeland proposals, reconstructed vocabulary, and limits of surviving early written evidence.

sources.title: On the origin of the ethnonym Tungus
sources.note: Russian Academy linguistic study dating widespread Russian-source use of Tungus to the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

sources.title: Mohe
sources.note: Expert encyclopedia synthesis of Chinese naming, varied groups, seasonal movement, subsistence, textiles, horses, and relations with neighboring states.

sources.title: Mohe archaeological culture
sources.note: Expert archaeology synthesis distinguishing Naifeld, Troitsky, and other regional groups, pottery traditions, and debated historical associations.

sources.title: Ethnocultural Atlas of the Amur Region
sources.note: Amur State University museum atlas on settlements, tools, mixed economies, burials, and the regional archaeological evidence base.

sources.title: Economy of the early medieval population of Primorye
sources.note: Far Eastern Academy study of sixth to early eighth century agriculture, husbandry, hunting, fishing, shellfish, plants, and evidentiary limits.

sources.title: Paleodiet studies from the Troitskiy Mohe cemetery
sources.note: Stable carbon and nitrogen isotope study finding mostly animal protein and a smaller C3 plant contribution in one cemetery sample.

sources.title: Cranial study of Mohe remains from Troitskiy cemetery
sources.note: Small osteological study of five male and five female crania, useful mainly for exposing sample and inference limits.

sources.title: Early Medieval Jeweler’s Kit from the Western Amur Region
sources.note: Late ninth-century Osinovoye Ozero crucible, furnace, plaques, repeated recasting, and reconstruction of local metalworking practice.

sources.title: Nonferrous metal items from early medieval Amur sites
sources.note: Materials analysis of eighth to tenth century ornaments, coin evidence, metal purity, recycling, and long-distance stylistic connections.

sources.title: Early medieval fortifications in the Amur region
sources.note: Archaeological classification of promontory and valley fortresses, ramparts, gates, floodplain settings, and mixed Mohe and Balhae materials.

sources.title: A newly documented medieval fortified settlement on the Shilka
sources.note: Russian Academy field report on thirty semi-subterranean dwellings, linear planning, possible public space, and turn-of-millennium dating.

sources.title: Mohe and Jurchen archaeology
sources.note: Amur State University museum account of multiple burial practices, grave objects, cenotaphs, and local interpretive cautions.

sources.title: Naifeld and Troitsky groups of Mohe culture in the western Amur region
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of settlement forms, house construction, regional pottery, and exact Troitsky cemetery burial proportions.

sources.title: Troitsky cemetery ceramic assemblage
sources.note: Archaeological study of handmade vessels and thousands of fragments from an eighth to early eleventh century cemetery.

sources.title: Tang Huiyao, volume 96, Blackwater Mohe entry
sources.note: Chinese institutional history compiled by Wang Pu in 961, preserving outsider administrative language about Blackwater Mohe and Tang offices.

sources.title: Balhae and Heishui Mohe relations
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study arguing for layered, simultaneous Heishui relations with Balhae, Tang, and steppe powers rather than a simple sequence.

sources.title: Balhae Kingdom gallery
sources.note: National Museum of Korea overview of Balhae chronology, regional extent, capitals, institutions, art, and diplomatic exchange.

sources.title: Goryeo’s governance of the Jurchen
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study identifying the first documented Jurchen naming in 903 and later differentiated outsider classifications.

sources.title: Balhae
sources.note: Academy of Korean Studies expert chronology of Balhae, Tang recognition, regional politics, and Khitan conquest in 926.
